chapters.title: Chapter 254: Kent’s Sword Intent Theory
paragraphs: Kent didn’t hold back his intent, something he never planned to hide in the first place.
The Gate Master was keen on breaking him, but she failed to notice she was playing with a dragon. Kent had already conquered two Saintesses; a Gate Master wouldn’t be much of a hassle.
But while he was thinking of all kinds of dirty stuff he would do to that ass. The Gate Master was regretting her decision to walk in front of him.
But that wasn’t something she could do but just hope that one of these days, she would get her hands on him.
They moved through the Sword Gate for a couple of minutes due to how fast they were walking. It would have been great if they flew, but...
After passing through the Sword Gate, they stopped in front of a small waterfall. Inside the waterfall was a cave, and that cave acted as the doorway to the Sword Garden.
That place was something the previous sect master found while exploring an ancient ruin thousands of years ago.

It’s filled with sword energy, so the moment a swordsman steps in, their understanding of the sword will take a huge turn. It was as if the moment one entered there, their sword comprehension speed skyrockets.

"What do you plan on achieving there?" the Gate Master asked when they arrived at the waterfall. She may hate Kent for taking all the beauties for himself, but she has also dedicated her entire life to the sword.
She was like the Spear Saintess; her life was one of battles and training in the hope that she would one day rise to the peak of the sword path.
So while she wanted to cut Kent’s dick off, she also wouldn’t be selfish and choose not to offer her knowledge in the sword path to a disciple under her care.
"I want to gain enlightenment from my sword intent. I believe I have reached a stage where a little clarity wouldn’t hurt," Kent said.
"What stage have you reached?" she smirked, clearly sensing a Level 5 Enhanced Sword Intent from him.
"Have you ever wondered if sword intent can be more than just conveying the intent of a swordsman?" Kent asked, causing the smirk on Gate Master Mara’s face to disappear.
Kent smiled and then began to tell her his theory.

"Sword intent, as we know it, is the manifestation of a swordsman’s will, their resolve, and their understanding of the blade. But what if it’s more than that? What if sword intent isn’t just a reflection of the wielder, but a force that can shape reality itself?"
Gate Master Mara narrowed her eyes at him.
She had been where he was and thought of that, but she never seemed to see past what he had just said.
It is true; the sword’s intent is based on the swordsman’s will, understanding, and resolve. This is why, in the end, this intent becomes Sword Will. It’s the will of the swordsman.
So, if that is the case, why not go beyond just conveying one’s resolve and will? Why not make it a force on its own?

"Imagine the case where instead of the intent pressing down on the person, it instead shapes the reality around them. Imagine you pull out your sword, and time seems to slow down, or you pull out your sword, and reality seems to start to distort."
Kent let out his theory, but the Gate master was not about to assume it was possible.
"All you say is imagination. I was once like you. I imagined countless ways to do what you are thinking about now, but even after years, I couldn’t find an answer.
Of course, I wouldn’t lie if I said this is possible. It’s indeed possible since somebody once achieved something similar to what you’re saying," the Gate Master said.
"Really?" Kent’s eyes lit up.
This theory was something Jest once thought of when he was looking for a way to keep moving. So, if that was the case, why not try it?
It was a long shot, but it seemed he would make headway, considering someone had already achieved something similar.
Just like that, without them knowing, they started to develop an interest they both could talk extensively about.
Kent was now talking to the Gate master who wasn’t thinking about cutting of his arms and perhaps, his dick.
"Yes. This person was a darkness elemental user. So when she started thinking of what you are thinking now, she began to experiment. And she had her breakthrough.
The darkness element is a force on its own. There are many ways to use it, so she harnessed one of those forces and imbued it into her intent.

So, this powerful force influences the intent whenever she pulls out her sword and emits her intent. So, in a way, she did something similar to what you are saying now. But that was her using an element.
Your thinking, the reason why I said it is just imagination, is because you are just thinking of what can be there, but not what is.
If you somehow manage to incorporate time into your intent, that would be good, but do you know how time works..."
The Gate Master was thorough. She knew this should be said to Kent so he would not waste his two days inside the garden.
"But imagination is just a way for us to create something great. I may not know how time works yet, but I have thousands of years ahead of me to figure it out. So I wouldn’t give up just yet."
Kent’s resolve was firm.
"You’re either a madman or a genius. Either way, I can’t deny that your words have sparked something in me. If you truly believe this is possible, then perhaps the Sword Garden is the place to start.
But know this, Kent—if you’re wrong, you’ll only waste your time. And if you’re right... well, you might just change the way we cultivate our sword intents, perhaps creating something new."
A small smile appeared on her face as she said that. Kent had indeed sparked something she had long given up on within her.
"You should smile more, Gate Master. Those dimples should be put on display more," Kent said, smiling at her cute expression, which vanished instantly, replaced by a glare.
"The gate is open. Know that after two days, you will be teleported outside regardless of what you are doing in there. I will wait for you here."
Kent nodded and flew toward the waterfall. The moment he passed through, he appeared inside the cave and slowly entered the garden through a portal.

chapters.title: Chapter 255: The Sword Garden
paragraphs: The moment Kent walked through the portal, he appeared inside a lush green garden filled with sword energy.
The energy of the sword is something no swordsman would run from. It’s just there, and when sensed, it means you are indeed walking the path of the sword.
A spearman wouldn’t feel anything if they found themselves there; they would only feel a warm breeze passing through their face.
They wouldn’t feel the sword intent in the air. Though faint, they wouldn’t feel the strands of the sword Will hidden within the sword energy.
Kent was basically standing inside a domain where his swordsmanship could take a huge turn if he desired.
The whole place was lush and beautiful.
The energy in the air was also very potent.
Kent smiled, looking around him.
"Focus and Enlightenment. Sounds easy to me," Kent said, walking toward a brownstone with a flat surface. He sat down and took out his sword, laying it before him.
He closed his eyes and began meditating, focusing on sword intent and his understanding so far.
Well, in a certain part of the memories he got from Jest, he had gained enlightenment when he was still a Sword Master heading toward the Sword Grandmaster stage.
Back then, he had witnessed a sword fight to the death between two Sword Saints. Through the battle, he gained clarity on how to harness sword intent more actively.
It wasn’t the theory he had discussed with the Gate Master. This was different from what he thought of, but Kent seemed to think it would be a start.
He wanted to understand how he could achieve the concept of harnessing sword intent to enhance his sword qi.
That was the first step.
He hadn’t told the Gate Master because he still did not trust her. He would worm his way into her heart and eventually strike, but for now, trust wasn’t something he would give easily.
So he sat down and began comprehending the memories from back then.
If he managed to gain some clarity from that, he would be able to attain enlightenment and eventually gain something he could use to begin walking the path she had theorized.
An hour passed, but nothing changed.
Kent was just sitting there with his eyes closed. Nothing changed, not even his aura.
The second hour came, and still, there was no change. Kent remained seated, which continued for ten hours with nothing new changing about him. In fact, his aura remained the same.
However, in the 11th hour, his aura—or, more importantly, his intent—started to surge. It began to rise, and from the energy it contained, the only thing that could be felt was a sense of sharpness.
Seventeen hours later, Kent opened his eyes and smiled.
"I don’t need enlightenment now; I need to understand how he did it," Kent said to himself, remembering the arcs that rained down on him when he challenged the Sword Bridge.
The clone was just too devastating.
"His arcs were sturdier and much more refined than mine. I couldn’t see how he did it back then, but I do now.
It was because the clone was using his sword qi with his intent. So, though those were just sword qi fashioned into arcs, they contained more than just sword qi.
They contained Sword Intent"
Kent gained clarity, and for that, he was happy.
The maximum for that skill was 450 arcs. So far, he had been able to unleash 230. However, now he knew what had to be done to make even the 230 more sturdy.
"I really don’t need the enlightenment simply because I don’t qualify for it. I mean, how was I expecting enlightenment when I don’t even have this much knowledge?"
He drew his sword, raising his intent and qi to the next level. Then he took just a single swing of his sword, causing 10 sword arcs to appear.
"As expected, it was indeed just the qi," Kent smiled. Then he took another swing, this time trying to add intent to it. However, it was easier said than done.
But Kent didn’t give up. He knew he had messed up when he failed to notice that the clone was actually using both qi and intent.
If he had known, he would have used the [Perfect Sword View] to master it.
It was one of the items he received when he awakened the Sword Tower. This sword view allows him to see the perfect form of a sword skill or technique and even how to master it.
Obviously, he wouldn’t be handed things on a silver platter. No, he would have to comprehend and practice what he saw until he mastered it.
The only advantage here is knowing that this is the perfect form and how to get there. Aside from that, he would need his own understanding.
But if that were the case, he would have by now mastered the intent infused into sword qi to make it much stronger and deadlier.

[It’s good to see the master finally appreciating what I gave him. You should make good use of the tools. You have the [Sword of Enlightenment], which is better than this place when you use it to comprehend something.
Besides that, you also have the Stone of Enlightenment, which I have moved to the front of the Sword of Enlightenment. If you put these two together, this garden will just be a rookie item.]
Gaia seemed to be waiting for this moment so she could rub it in his face.
Kent knew he deserved that. He indeed had the perfect tools inside the Sword Gate.
Aside from wanting to spar with his master and Neomi, he had an item inside the tower that allowed him to challenge powerful swordsmen in a dream-like state.
But besides that, he could easily gain enlightenment on the Stone of Enlightenment while using the Sword of Enlightenment.
If he wanted to master a skill or a technique, he could just use the Perfect Sword View for that. Basically, he had no use for this place.
"But I am here, and it’s here I gained the clarity, so if there is another chance to enter here, I wouldn’t bat an eye. But since I am here now, I might as well make good use of it."

chapters.title: Chapter 256: A Sword Genius
paragraphs: Kent set the sword down and went into a meditative posture.
He was using the Sword Mind to comprehend the clarity he had received. The fusion of sword intent with Sword Qi is the first step toward something much bigger.
So, he was making sure his understanding at the foundational stage was solid. This is why, instead of doing trial and error, he was using the Sword Mind to create a foundation he would build upon.
A couple of hours passed, but he was merely thinking and creating countless scenarios in his head. This continued until a day passed inside the garden.
That was when he opened his eyes and took his sword again.
This time, instead of just swinging it, he held the hilt of his sword with his right hand and the sheath with his left hand and closed his eyes.
His intent surged, and the Qi danced across the sword.
Then suddenly, his eyes snapped open, and he pulled out the sword into a swing, returning it to the sheath less than a second later.
It was a quick attack that was just too fast to comprehend, yet 100 sword arcs flashed out, decimating a part of the garden.
It healed back the next second.
"Damn, that’s what I’m talking about!" Kent jumped into the air, beaming with happiness. He had executed his first attack with intent and sword qi fused together.
The attack was as he wanted it. Of course, it was just the initial stage, but it was progress nonetheless.
It was an achievement worth celebrating.
"But comparing this to that of the clone, I need to improve 80% more and add 220 more arcs to my 230 arcs to be able to counter his attacks the next time we face off."
"I won’t lose in the next challenge even though the difficulty has been raised by 1"

Kent resolved himself and started practicing the sword even more. The more he practiced, the better he got. Four hours into the second day, he was able to improve to at least 80% of the clone’s standards.

He then went back into the meditative posture and began comprehending this process even further. The feeling coming from each swing was just too enticing, so he was doing everything possible to handle this task well.
His motivation came from the fact that Jest wasn’t able to create a presence for sword intent like he was now thinking of doing.
Jest, the same Jest he remembered, his past self was a genius with the sword.
Comparing the current him to his former self was like an insult. But he was the same person, and that genius gene ran through them.
So, something that was started by his past must be completed well. This means all the genius of Jest was now with him, and that is being assimilated into his own genius.
From what he had sensed so far, the more he wielded and practiced the sword, the more he grew.
So Kent wasn’t holding back; he wanted to gain something at least so he and the gate master could have something to obsess over when he trusted her enough.
Of course, his intentions are anything but pure.
...it’s always the endgame that counts.
If only the gate master knew she was being used as motivation by a certain purple-haired brat, she would probably expel him from the sect.
Kent was now seeing the allure of having multiple women all linked to his tower. Aside from the intimacy, his strength never seemed to lack. He kept receiving something from them.
So now, if he was going to walk this path, then he would walk it with naked bodies filling his bed.
An orgy session here and there wouldn’t be a bad thing at all.
Ten hours into the second day, Kent opened his eyes and started practicing again. This time, he was much more experienced with swinging his sword.
He wasn’t just randomly swinging it... this shows he was growing.
In the 12th hour, he executed the first perfect Rapid Sword strike, and it was beautiful.
[Congratulations, Master. Your understanding of the sword has increased by 10%.]
Kent smiled upon seeing this. He was rather happy he was able to do something like this within a day and a half.
However, he never expected a boost from that.
Yet, his mind had opened even more, causing him to understand something finally.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
"The more sword arcs I create from here onwards, the more my understanding will expand. This begs the question: is 450 the max for the sword arcs, or is it much more than that?"
Kent seemed to have gained another clarity; this time, he wanted to see it through to the end.
He began swinging his sword, causing sword arc after sword arc to rain down. The more arcs he created, the more his understanding of the technique seemed to grow.
Kent was elated, so he never stopped and kept going for hours until Gaia suddenly reminded him he had only 5 minutes before he would be kicked out.
He stopped and sighed.
Then he took one last swing, sending 380 sword arcs flying. A smile tugged at his lips. He had come for enlightenment, but instead, he was leaving with something much more profound.
In a way, he had been enlightened on how to walk the path he had envisioned.
He now understood how to fuse intent into sword qi—even if he was only at the initial stage.
"The next step would be to fuse an element into it. This will give me two fields to study, and from there, I can figure out a way to create a presence for it.
Though it’s not going to be easy—simply because it hasn’t been achieved yet—I will walk this path and make it a reality. This way, I will once again become a progenitor."
Kent smiled.
What he was planning to achieve was fusing a law into his sword.
He may have seen it as wanting to fuse it into the sword intent, but in reality, he would be fusing it into the sword itself...
So, in a way, with a swing, if he manages to infuse the law of time into his sword, he can either slow down the space around his opponent or speed it up.
In a way, Kent was thinking of the impossible—something that had been abandoned by some of the greatest swordsmen to have ever walked this path and those who still walk it.
But if he were to achieve that, it would be both genius and deadly. Instead of relying on skill, he would now be relying on a law—or laws, if he learns more than one.
’Imagine a sword intent imbued with the power of death,’ Kent thought, smiling as he was teleported out.

chapters.title: Chapter 257: How Did It Go...
paragraphs: "How did it go?" Master Mara asked the moment Kent appeared outside. It had already been two days, and as she had promised, she waited for him until he came out.
"It went well," Kent responded. "Though I couldn’t gain enlightenment like I hoped, I did gain something much more valuable."
"That is good then... I guess you didn’t waste your chance there, as most do," she said.
"I guess so too," Kent replied. He wasn’t sure if he should talk to her about his breakthrough in the garden.
The discovery that he could use his sword intent with qi for active attacks wasn’t something entirely new, but perhaps the way he understood it was something many would cherish.
He observed her expression, trying to see if she was curious about his breakthrough, but he saw nothing of the sort. In the end, Kent decided to keep the matter to himself and move on.
If there came a time when she gained his trust, he might share his discovery with her. But for now, Kent would keep it to himself.
It was selfish in a way, but she is a Sword Sage; she has more knowledge than him, so Kent was also lacking.
But he has the power to do that. He has the tower on his side. Then again, the gate master cannot go into the tower either.
He cannot take her to the tower without her gaining his trust by either being in his harem, his servant, or part of his legion.
Li Hua is there because she is just a kid, and even though she is under his protection, she is part of the guardian tower.
"By the way, where is your master?" she asked. She could tell Kent had made some progress merely by looking at him, but she also did not see him sharing simply because she wouldn’t share.
’His aura is different. I guess he is a genius, just like his master,’ she said to herself.
"Master is in closed-door seclusion," Kent replied.
"Tell her to come see me when she comes out..." She wanted to continue with something but stopped herself.
"I will pass on your message," Kent replied. He also saw she wanted to say something, but since she was not willing to talk, he would just keep quiet.
"By the way, Gate Master, I heard there are still two spots reserved for the upcoming Sect competition," Kent said with a small smile.
"Don’t tell me you want to join," she said, though she knew his answer.

"It’s only natural for me to join if this sect has a chance at winning. I mean, I defeated a Spear Saint just a couple of days ago. So, from where I stand, I am more than qualified. He is even on the roster to represent the sect...so."
Kent wasn’t about to think she was his friend, but he also couldn’t help being himself around her. That’s just the way he is.
The Gate master was at the Root Transcendent stage, just a step away from breaking through to the Root Ascension stage.
Someone like her should be feared, but in Kent’s eye, she is just an uptight beauty waiting for someone to put her on all four and fuck her well.
Obviously, he thinks he is that destined person.
The gate master didn’t see it that way though...she was rather amused by Kent’s statement.
"Wait, you think the sect is basing its winning on that brat or the disciple of the Spear Gate?" the Gate Master sneered.

"The sect has hidden monsters. The competition only requires nine active participants after the first challenge, and let me tell you, we have Nine of them, and each is on the same level as your master.
The only reason your master or the Spear Saintess wouldn’t be participating is because of their status as Saintesses."
"So, tell me, Kent, can you defeat your master?" she asked with a smirk.
Kent scratched his head, knowing full well that he wouldn’t be able to defeat his master.
Saintess Selene may pale in comparison to her sister Neomi, but she is in no way weak. Kent wouldn’t be able to defeat her.
"Then this means even if I somehow get one of the two spots left, when the time comes, I wouldn’t be allowed to fight actively," Kent said.
"That is exactly what I mean," she responded, but Kent just sighed.
"Looks like I must challenge my master to a duel and wipe her face on the floor," he chuckled, knowing what he must do next.
The Gate Master just smirked, but she didn’t put much thought into what Kent had just said. If only she knew the brat was actually serious.
Right now, he wanted to face monsters, and what better way to do that than a competition where only the best of the best would be participating?
Also, if he wants to have a chance at defeating his master, now is the best time.
The moment she starts walking the Primordial Sword Path he had made for her, things will be different. It will take him some time before he can catch up to her.
"Go back and use this time to ponder your breakthrough. Since you are now a disciple in the Sword Gate, you can book a room at the Sword Tower.
Then, use the time to ponder your breakthrough. This way, though you are out of the Garden, you still wouldn’t lack inside the towers."
The gate master offered her advice like any gate master would.
Every gate in the sect has a tower—the Sword Tower, the Spear Tower, or even the Archer Tower.
So, though Kent also has his overpowered tower, the sect also has formations that help speed up cultivation and practice.
But Kent wasn’t about to go there when he had the best thing. He has all the time inside the tower, so what waste it on trivial towers like the one the sect has?
His tower is the best, and so he wouldn’t leave that place. The sect can keep their towers to themselves.
"I will listen to your advice, Gate Master," Kent, of course, wasn’t about to reject the offer. That would be impolite. So after saying that, he left the Gate Master alone.
Clearly, she had learned her lesson, so she wasn’t about to walk in front of him. She wouldn’t give him that show again.
But that wasn’t going to be easy. After moving a few steps, Kent turned around and took out a wine from his space ring.
Of course, it was actually from his tower storage, but he made it appear as though it came from his storage ring.
"Take this. It seemed to have helped you before. But just so you know, my offer still stands—just one massage, and you’ll come running for more next time."
After saying that, he left and headed straight back to the mansion. He then entered the tower, went straight to the Stone of Enlightenment, and began practicing the Sword Mind.
He had 24 days to get things done there. By then, a day would have passed on the outside. Ingrid and her master would be done by then.

chapters.title: Chapter 258: Mastering Rapid Slash
paragraphs: It had already been 12 days since Kent began practicing the sword mind inside the tower. The past 12 days had been spent mastering the 10,002 sword plays using his mind.
Before entering, he had only mastered 700 out of the 10,002, but now, after breaking through inside the sword garden and receiving the boost afterward, his pace had picked up.
So far, he has mastered 4,560 sword plays. This caused his Enhanced Sword Qi and intent at level 5 to shoot up to level 6 and even started approaching level 7th level.
But Kent stopped when he reached 4,600.
The sword mind wasn’t the reason he had come there.
It was merely his way of taking his mastery to the next level while checking to see if his focus passive skill was indeed a thing.
"The focus passive skill is great, alright," Kent said, standing up.
He walked away, contemplating how best to proceed with his chances of gaining his first enlightenment.
According to both Gaia and his master, gaining enlightenment adds to a person’s strength. It’s like opening up one potential even further...
Fighting someone who had gained enlightenment in a certain aspect of the sword was something worth taking seriously, or else he might just lose.
So he was now heading in the direction where his enlightenment should be near.
Then again, he was forgetting the path he was walking. The Genesis Path was no easy path. Of course, if he were to gain enlightenment, his mastery would take a new leap.
"I can feel it. The enlightenment will come soon. I just have to master the Rapid Sword Slash to a certain stage and see if that will allow me to see the next path after the intent and Qi infusion."
He made his way to the Perfect Sword View, where he planned to use it well. It was one of the cool stuff Gaia created for him.
"Gaia," Kent called out, and the cosmic loli appeared the next second.

[Looks like you finally want to make good use of all the amazing things I created. It took me countless prototypes and research to make this. I had to scout thousands of galaxies just for the schematics.]
The cute little lollipop spoke, making Kent curl his mouth into a smirk.
"Then it means there are exactly the same things somewhere in the universe since the schematics are not yours," he said, making Gaia clench her little fist.
She then pointed her little finger at Kent.
[Listen here, Master, I am a cosmic weaver. Whatever I create is one of a kind. I may have seen schematics for this capsule and room design, but everything else is me.
There is only one [Perfect Sword View], and it’s what you have here. So appreciate my hard work.] Kent just smiled, knowing full well she was serious by the look on her face.
Gaia had been frustrated seeing Kent not taking her creations seriously, so she finally vented her frustration in the cutest way possible.

"The next time you want to say something serious, try to look less cute and beautiful and more mature and serious. The current you is not giving the ’if you don’t pay attention to my creations, I will send you on a deadly quest’ vibe."
"You..." Gaia wanted to punch the brat, but Akira appeared the next second, stopping her overly impulsive sister, who would accidentally destroy the tower if she were offended.
Though she wasn’t about to destroy something she had spent millions of years creating, she would indeed make Kent scream a bit.
"Just sit inside, and a panel of all your sword skills will appear. Select the one you want, and you will enter the simulation."
In the end, she is Gaia, someone who is all about ensuring her master is happy and has all he needs.
"Thank you, Madam Gaia. I will reward you later when I leave here. How about a stroll through the other gates? Does that sound good?"
"You better," she said, then vanished, leaving only Akira behind. She just smiled and decided to do damage control for her sister.
"We didn’t want to tell you, but our last sibling may have just gotten herself into trouble. As the cosmic weaver, Gaia was able to see what she was going through and where she was.
So she’s just grumpy. But don’t worry—that bitch wouldn’t die even if a celestial god attacked her. When you’re strong enough, we’ll go rescue her."
After saying that, she also left.
"There’s another one of them? I wonder if she’s also a loli," Kent mused with a smile, though he didn’t dwell on it.
He would ask them for more clarity on what exactly their sister had gotten herself into.
He entered the capsule resembling a chair, and something akin to a futuristic glass covered his face. The next second, he was standing in the air with a sea below him and mountains all around.
[Welcome to the Perfect Sword View. You may select the skill you want to master]
→ String Sovereign Strike
→ Annihilation Sword
→ Nine Calamities sword strike
→ Void Cutter
→ Elemental Lord
"Looks like only sword skills can be mastered here. I will have to ask Gaia to create one for the other skills," Kent said, and then he selected the Annihilation Sword.
In the next second, the first form of the technique was activated: [Rapid Slash].
An identical copy of Kent appeared, holding a white sword. He then looked toward a certain mountain and made a single swing. But that was enough.
One hundred sword arcs appeared and rained down on the mountain, sending shockwaves far and wide. Kent’s eyes narrowed, and a smile appeared on his lips.
He saw it—he saw how the energy moved into the sword, how it interacted with the intent in the air, and how it was infused.
He saw how the clone activated the hundred arcs... It was like he was the one doing it. It felt like he was the one who took the swing.
It felt surreal.
"This is the best," Kent was overjoyed. The feeling was something he only needed a few swings to master.
The clone took another swing, and 200 arcs appeared. Kent felt that, too, and then he continued to observe as the clone went until 450 arcs appeared.
He then went back to 100 again. He went through the sequence three more times. Then when he came back for a 4th, Kent changed strategy.
This time, Kent sat down in the air and closed his eyes. Instead of looking at the clone, he was rather feeling him.
It was something he never knew was possible, but now that he was doing it, he could already sense his understanding expanding.
’I need this,’ Kent said. And so, for six whole days, he just sat there, feeling everything inside his body, mind, and even down to his soul.
After six days, he mastered the skill without even taking up his sword. He had already mastered it mentally, and his body adapted to it thanks to his unique Dragon physique and cultivation technique.
His path also played a role.
When he stopped the simulation and came out, he quickly went to the Eternal Sword Arena and unsheathed his sword.
He sighed, and then he took a single swing, and 200 arcs appeared. He smiled and started swinging more. This took him only a few seconds until all 450 arcs appeared.
When the 450 arcs appeared, Kent felt like that was the limit. It was strange, but it felt like that was all he could handle.
It was as if all his energy and blood vessels were meant to only be able to handle 450 arcs.
’Then I declare, I will break this barrier on my own if I want to win against the clone. I need to have something he can’t replicate.’
He looked toward the Sword Bridge and sighed.
’I will be coming soon.’

sentences.text: It had already been 12 days since Kent began practicing the sword mind inside the tower.
The past 12 days had been spent mastering the 10,002 sword plays using his mind.
Before entering, he had only mastered 700 out of the 10,002, but now, after breaking through inside the sword garden and receiving the boost afterward, his pace had picked up.
So far, he has mastered 4,560 sword plays.
This caused his Enhanced Sword Qi and intent at level 5 to shoot up to level 6 and even started approaching level 7th level.
But Kent stopped when he reached 4,600.
The sword mind wasn’t the reason he had come there.
It was merely his way of taking his mastery to the next level while checking to see if his focus passive skill was indeed a thing.
"The focus passive skill is great, alright," Kent said, standing up.
He walked away, contemplating how best to proceed with his chances of gaining his first enlightenment.
According to both Gaia and his master, gaining enlightenment adds to a person’s strength.
It’s like opening up one potential even further...
Fighting someone who had gained enlightenment in a certain aspect of the sword was something worth taking seriously, or else he might just lose.
So he was now heading in the direction where his enlightenment should be near.
Then again, he was forgetting the path he was walking.
The Genesis Path was no easy path.
Of course, if he were to gain enlightenment, his mastery would take a new leap.
"I can feel it.
The enlightenment will come soon.
I just have to master the Rapid Sword Slash to a certain stage and see if that will allow me to see the next path after the intent and Qi infusion."
He made his way to the Perfect Sword View, where he planned to use it well.
It was one of the cool stuff Gaia created for him.
"Gaia," Kent called out, and the cosmic loli appeared the next second.
[Looks like you finally want to make good use of all the amazing things I created.
It took me countless prototypes and research to make this.
I had to scout thousands of galaxies just for the schematics.]
The cute little lollipop spoke, making Kent curl his mouth into a smirk.
"Then it means there are exactly the same things somewhere in the universe since the schematics are not yours," he said, making Gaia clench her little fist.
She then pointed her little finger at Kent.
[Listen here, Master, I am a cosmic weaver.
Whatever I create is one of a kind.
I may have seen schematics for this capsule and room design, but everything else is me.
There is only one [Perfect Sword View], and it’s what you have here.
So appreciate my hard work.] Kent just smiled, knowing full well she was serious by the look on her face.
Gaia had been frustrated seeing Kent not taking her creations seriously, so she finally vented her frustration in the cutest way possible.
"The next time you want to say something serious, try to look less cute and beautiful and more mature and serious.
The current you is not giving the ’if you don’t pay attention to my creations, I will send you on a deadly quest’ vibe."
"You..." Gaia wanted to punch the brat, but Akira appeared the next second, stopping her overly impulsive sister, who would accidentally destroy the tower if she were offended.
Though she wasn’t about to destroy something she had spent millions of years creating, she would indeed make Kent scream a bit.
"Just sit inside, and a panel of all your sword skills will appear.
Select the one you want, and you will enter the simulation."
In the end, she is Gaia, someone who is all about ensuring her master is happy and has all he needs.
"Thank you, Madam Gaia.
I will reward you later when I leave here.
How about a stroll through the other gates?
Does that sound good?"
"You better," she said, then vanished, leaving only Akira behind.
She just smiled and decided to do damage control for her sister.
"We didn’t want to tell you, but our last sibling may have just gotten herself into trouble.
As the cosmic weaver, Gaia was able to see what she was going through and where she was.
So she’s just grumpy.
But don’t worry—that bitch wouldn’t die even if a celestial god attacked her.
When you’re strong enough, we’ll go rescue her."
After saying that, she also left.
"There’s another one of them?
I wonder if she’s also a loli," Kent mused with a smile, though he didn’t dwell on it.
He would ask them for more clarity on what exactly their sister had gotten herself into.
He entered the capsule resembling a chair, and something akin to a futuristic glass covered his face.
The next second, he was standing in the air with a sea below him and mountains all around.
[Welcome to the Perfect Sword View.
You may select the skill you want to master]
→ String Sovereign Strike
→ Annihilation Sword
→ Nine Calamities sword strike
→ Void Cutter
→ Elemental Lord
"Looks like only sword skills can be mastered here.
I will have to ask Gaia to create one for the other skills," Kent said, and then he selected the Annihilation Sword.
In the next second, the first form of the technique was activated: [Rapid Slash].
An identical copy of Kent appeared, holding a white sword.
He then looked toward a certain mountain and made a single swing.
But that was enough.
One hundred sword arcs appeared and rained down on the mountain, sending shockwaves far and wide.
Kent’s eyes narrowed, and a smile appeared on his lips.
He saw it—he saw how the energy moved into the sword, how it interacted with the intent in the air, and how it was infused.
He saw how the clone activated the hundred arcs...
It was like he was the one doing it.
It felt like he was the one who took the swing.
It felt surreal.
"This is the best," Kent was overjoyed.
The feeling was something he only needed a few swings to master.
The clone took another swing, and 200 arcs appeared.
Kent felt that, too, and then he continued to observe as the clone went until 450 arcs appeared.
He then went back to 100 again.
He went through the sequence three more times.
Then when he came back for a 4th, Kent changed strategy.
This time, Kent sat down in the air and closed his eyes.
Instead of looking at the clone, he was rather feeling him.
It was something he never knew was possible, but now that he was doing it, he could already sense his understanding expanding.
’I need this,’ Kent said.
And so, for six whole days, he just sat there, feeling everything inside his body, mind, and even down to his soul.
After six days, he mastered the skill without even taking up his sword.
He had already mastered it mentally, and his body adapted to it thanks to his unique Dragon physique and cultivation technique.
His path also played a role.
When he stopped the simulation and came out, he quickly went to the Eternal Sword Arena and unsheathed his sword.
He sighed, and then he took a single swing, and 200 arcs appeared.

This took him only a few seconds until all 450 arcs appeared.
When the 450 arcs appeared, Kent felt like that was the limit.
It was strange, but it felt like that was all he could handle.
It was as if all his energy and blood vessels were meant to only be able to handle 450 arcs.
’Then I declare, I will break this barrier on my own if I want to win against the clone.
I need to have something he can’t replicate.’
He looked toward the Sword Bridge and sighed.
’I will be coming soon.’

chapters.title: Chapter 259: Challenging a Rude Sword Saintess
paragraphs: Kent had finally mastered the Rapid Slash, which is the first form of the Annihilation sword technique. This was a huge deal for him, considering his sword intent and sword qi has now reached the 6th level.
The quest to fuse the sword with the sword qi had also improved to 85% already, so he was basically at the peak of that sword skill.
However, what made Kent stay up for 6 whole days just thinking was the fact that after he mastered the skill which saw him unleashing 450 sword arcs with a single swing, his limit was reached.
It was like his body had reached the limit it could function with that skill. So for now, Kent who saw the need to surpass this stage was now thinking of how to push his body beyond that.
So the last 6 days was him just sitting in the [Stone of Enlightenment], thinking.
For now, he had only done loads of thinking. But in the process, he gains clarity, pushing the fusion to 95%, almost at the peak where he will then see if his enlightenment will show or not.
After six days, he stood up and was ready to head to the sword bridge and blow off some steam. However, before he can even take a single step, Gaia appears in front of him.
"We have a problem master," She said plainly.

"What is it?" Kent asked. Right now, he wanted only one thing, and that was to fight something. Though he couldn’t break the limit, he was now confident he would win simply due to his sudden level-up and the stat points left to add.
He didn’t think the bridge would also have an undistributed point system, so he wanted to use that when needed.
Of course, even if the clone copied that too, he was confident this time. He was ready to handle the first challenge.
But Gaia’s warning was also important, so he had to hold back and listen first.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞

"Some sword saintess by the name of Val is at the gate of the Sword Gate, badmouthing your master and asking the sect to present the one they are calling the Monster of Sword Gate. She is asking for you."
"Is that so?" He sighs
"Very well, I will go greet her," Kent said. He changed his plans and left the tower. This lady seemed like the perfect stepping stone for him.
At the Sword Gate entrance, a striking beauty with blonde hair and brown eyes could be seen sneering at the elders facing her in what seemed to be a standoff.
It’s even weird to say she was the one winning, considering she held a sneer while the elders wore a frown. The verbal battle wasn’t going their way... not even in the slightest.
The lady they are facing is Sword Saintess Val from the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect. They are the number one sword sect in the entire Athea Kingdom and perhaps the entire four kingdoms.
This lady, however, is one of the five swords Saintess the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect had produced. She is talented with the sword, and so is she with her mouth.
They said when you face her in battle, just her vulgar words are enough to make you wish for her to stab you through the heart and be done with it.
Her words are rather dehumanizing.

"Old Lu, I heard the reason you couldn’t settle down was because your second sword couldn’t handle the sword qi like your fellow men. Do you perhaps need me to cut the burden off?" she asked, causing an elder to grit his teeth.
"Gritting your teeth wouldn’t fix the gaps in them," she added, making Elder Lu want to move and give her a good smacking.
Sword Saintess Val just smiled.
She came to the Sword Gate mainly for two things. First, she wanted to challenge Saintess Selene, who had already defeated her twice.
Of course, she wasn’t convinced, so she came for her when she got the chance to leave the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect.
The second was to find a way to bring Kent to their side. The Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect is a place where only swordsmen can be found.
In fact, they hated Kent, but if he were to join them, he would be treated like a delicate flower.
That is how much they cherish their disciples. It’s either you join them or die.
She wanted to make a bet with Saintess Selene: if she won the duel, Kent would become her disciple and join the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect.
So, until Saintess Selene came out, she wouldn’t stop insulting the Sword Gate elders.
Thus, the Gate Master, who knew her character, chose not to come out and continued to watch from afar as the loudmouth Saintess bathed her elders in all kinds of mud.
This had been going on for 20 whole minutes until Gaia went to call Kent. Now, the elders were losing all restraint, and if they weren’t held back, they might just commit murder.

"I’ve seen a lot of cowards for Lord knows how long, but this is my first time seeing a sect full of cowards portrayed as sect elders. I have to say, I look down on the Sword Gate and the sect as a whole," she sneered.
The elders were finally fed up, so they drew their weapons and were about to lunge at her when a calm yet arrogant voice spoke.

"I’ve seen loads of ugly bitches in my time, and let me tell you, I’ve lived for 18 years already, but this is my first time seeing a beautiful lady who is ugly on the inside. I have to say, my eyes are opened today," Kent said, walking forward with a calm expression on his face.
The Saintess, who had just been insulted on a soul-deep level, narrowed her eyes at the handsome fellow who had appeared.
"You’re him," she said, looking hungrily at Kent.
"I was told you were badmouthing my master. Care to explain why?" Kent asked.
"Because I came for your head. If she dares to accept and loses, you will become my disciple and forever be my servant," she arrogantly declared.
Kent smirked and said, "My master doesn’t accept challenges from weaklings, but since you’re here, I can only discipline you for insulting my seniors."
Kent spoke like a righteous monk, but his gaze said, *I dare you to accept.*

chapters.title: Chapter 260: High Stake Bet
paragraphs: A small smile appeared on Gate Master Mara’s lips when she heard Kent’s words. She was about 3 km away, but she could hear everything clearly as if she were right there.
She heard every vulgar word spoken by the Sword Saintess.
Though she knew her character, she was still irritated by how she was disrespecting the elders. If she could, she would have killed her long ago.
But that would create too much trouble.
However, now she doesn’t have to do anything. Kent, who knew how to use his tongue, was already doing the damage control for her.
"You, a mere grandmaster swordsman, want to challenge a whole Sword Saintess to a duel. Are you perhaps having a dream?" she asked with laughter.
"I can think clearly, and from where I stand, I don’t see much. All I see is a lady who thinks she is better than everyone, yet she is nothing in the grand scheme of things.
But that can be fixed if only you have the balls... ahem... boobs to accept my challenge. Emphasis on the boobs part,"
Kent said with a teasing smile. This seemed to have struck a chord, making her frown. Although the lady in front of him was a beauty, her chest wasn’t that encouraging.
"You are arrogant," she said. Kent just reminded her why she hated his master. They both are beauties with good backsides, but her chest pales in comparison.
"I know," Kent replied, looking narrowly at the lady.
"I accept your challenge. However, I have a request, and you cannot say no to it," she said, making Kent smile inwardly.
"Tell me. If it’s within my capabilities, I will do it," Kent said.
"Let’s make a bet. If you lose, you will become my disciple and leave the Divine Palace Sect for the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect," she said, making Kent smirk.

"Though you don’t have what it takes to become my master, I will accept your bet. However, if I win, you will become my servant for 100 years and, like you said, you will leave the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect and join the Divine Palace Sect,"
Kent said, and the Saintess narrowed her eyes.
"Don’t go too far, brat. What do you take me for? Change the stakes, for though you would lose, thinking of making me your servant is the last thing I want."
"So you are afraid of losing. For someone who thinks she is better than everyone, why worry about a simple bet?" Kent asked.

For some reason, the Saintess didn’t like how confident Kent was. It was as if he had everything figured out and thought he was in control. It was like he had already won the duel even before it started.

’There is no way to enforce it, so he can’t just do anything if he wins. Fuck, why am I thinking I will lose when I am clearly the one at an advantage here?’ She practically hated her brain at the moment.
This caused her to glare at Kent, who just stood there watching her.
"Fine. I accept your bet." Since there was no way to enforce it, she could only say that and figure out the rest later.
Well, that was how it was supposed to go, but then Kent produced two contracts from thin air and handed them to her.
"This contract will enforce the bets. If any of us goes against the stakes we have stated, our soul will undergo extreme torture every two hours until we accept our loss and do as the bet states."
Kent said, making the Saintess look at him weirdly.

In the end, she didn’t believe the contrast could enforce the bets, so she signed with her blood. If only she knew Akira was the one behind the contract. Then again, she had never met a soul weaver before.
The contract now allows Akira to do as she pleases the moment any of them go against the stakes they set after the duel.
Kent is confident, and so is the lady, but Kent is no easy person. He had finally made a breakthrough, and so, he planned on testing his limits and even distributing his points accordingly.

"Elders, please take her to the arena. I have something to do and will head there immediately after." The elders, who were saved from the embarrassment Val was putting them through, were more than happy to lead her away.
A few seconds later, the Gate Master appeared.
"Are you being serious now? You do know if you lose, you will become her disciple and forever leave your master," she asked in an angry tone.
For someone who wanted Kent gone, this should be the happiest moment for her. However, she doesn’t seem to be happy about the decision Kent made, accepting such a bet from the crazy Saintess.
She may be a loudmouth, but she is in no way weak.

"I don’t plan on losing, Gate Master. Although she is a Root Great Sage and a Sword Saint, I plan on winning, and you will finally see that I qualify to be part of the nine active disciples you selected for the competition," Kent said, smiling.
"You are unbelievable," she said, shaking her head.
This was her first time meeting such an interesting guy. Kent may merely be a Root Sage, but he is not an easy cookie for the Saintess to crack.
The discovery that his sword intent and qi could be fused, coupled with the fact that he had mastered the rapid slash to that extent, gave him confidence.
But this is a duel between swordsmen. Kent may be at a disadvantage; however, he wasn’t in any way weaker.
With his skills higher than the maximum of this world, he was bound to make this lady regret the day she was born if she became careless.
"Does your master know you are doing something like this?" she asked.
"Master is still in seclusion, so this was my own idea. Don’t worry, I won’t put the sect to shame." After saying that, Kent began walking away.
The Gate Master stared at his back for a few minutes before sighing.
’He is clearly bold, but will that help him against that crazy lady who doesn’t play by the rules?’ she thought, and then she vanished from where she stood.

chapters.title: Chapter 261: Kent vs Sword Saintess Val (1)
paragraphs: "Have you heard?" a disciple asked his friend.
"Heard what?"
"That brat who won the Trial of the Sword just challenged the Sword Saintess from the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect to a sword duel."
"What?!" the friend exclaimed with a shocked expression.
This friend was the same Max who, out of greed, chose to enter the roster of the 100 disciples Kent traumatized—ahem—defeated during the Sword Trial.
He had been recovering after that battle, so he hadn’t come out to hear what was going on around the sect. However, just now, his friend arrived with another piece of news, and it was shocking.
Even more shocking than the challenge that took place weeks ago.
"Tell me it’s a lie," Max said.

"Can’t you see what’s going on outside?" his friend replied, causing Max to look out the window. True to his friend’s words, disciples could be seen moving toward the largest coliseum of the Sword Gate.
"I only came to tell you because I know you still haven’t recovered from that defeat. Perhaps, seeing him get trashed will make you feel better."
After saying that, the friend left, leaving Max to ponder what to do next.
Obviously, he followed suit. The allure of seeing Kent get trashed wasn’t something he or the others who were defeated during the Sword Trial would pass up on.
It took just two hours, but the arena was packed to the brim.
This was like a once-in-a-lifetime duel worth watching. Of course, they weren’t placing Kent in high regard. They knew he would get trashed.
The only reason they were there was because of the Saintess.
It’s rare to see a Saintess fight, so this was like an eye-opener for them. They wanted to see just how she would trash Kent and see if they could gain something from her mastery over the sword.
Inside the VIP room in the arena, Gate Master Mara, along with Gate Master Camilla, were seated and ready to watch the duel of the brat they were tasked with keeping alive.
"Your gate has become rather lively since that brat stepped in," Gate Master Camilla said, a smirk playing on her lips.
"Maybe not for long. After he gets trashed, he’ll calm down a bit. Well, he will be taken away so..." Gate Master Mara said indifferently.
"You don’t think that handsome brat will win?" Gate Master Camilla asked.

"Are you seriously asking that? He is merely a Grandmaster swordsman; how is he going to win against a Sword Saintess? I know Selene is more impressive than this bitch, but she is not to be underestimated," she said, making Gate Master Camilla nod.
"True, but where is the trust you should have for the disciple of your gate?"
"I shouldn’t even be here, considering the duel will end before it even starts," Gate Master Mara said indifferently again.

"Then why don’t we put some stakes on it? If your disciple loses, I fulfill a request from you, and if he somehow manages to win, you will let the brat accompany me on a mission," Gate Master Camilla said, smiling.
Her friend just looked at her with disdain. She is practically asking to spend some time with the brat, who only seems to attract trouble.
"Whatever makes you happy, I guess," she said. Of course, she accepted her request.
Gate Master Camilla smiled and focused on the arena, where the arrogant Sword Saintess appeared, riding on a thin sword.
Cheers followed her entry. Of course, it was to be expected, considering she is a Saintess and everyone respected her.
A few minutes after she entered, a bolt of lightning flashed through the entrance, and she stopped opposite the Saintess.
Then the bolt burst wide open, and from within the blast, Kent appeared, smiling back at the Saintess.
Everyone narrowed their eyes at the flashy entry Kent displayed. It was just too flashy to be taken seriously. Kent appeared like a tribulation, and with it, the duel was about to begin.
"If you don’t mind me asking, what would you do if you lose? Will you try to run?" Kent asked.
"I don’t need to run simply because you don’t have what it takes to defeat me. But fear not, I will make it quick."
A thin sword appeared in the air, and then two more followed, making it three. The Saintess then extended her hand, and another sword appeared in her firm grip.
[Fancy. Looks like she has mastered the art of spirit-wielding] Gaia said, amused for some reason.

Spirit-wielding is when a swordsman, spearman, or any weapon cultivator uses their mind to control their weapons. Right now, the Saintess was using three flying swords and a real sword in her grip for the battle.

Kent smiled. "A wise man once said, ’What shall it profit a woman if she had all the swords in the world but doesn’t know how to wield them?’" He took a step forward, causing the air to distort around him.
"I may be a Grandmaster, but there is another saying that goes, ’Don’t judge a book by its cover.’" He extended his hand, and the golden sword sheath appeared, causing many to raise their eyebrows.
"But you can judge now, for you wouldn’t have the same chance again. Not ever." Kent pointed the golden sheath at her and said the magic words.
"Give me your best swing... Saintess."

That was all it took, but the next second, three swords came from three different directions. The speed was just too much to handle. However, Kent just took a single swing, and three sword arcs appeared.
The three thin flying swords were countered, and then he blinked away and appeared behind the Saintess. However, before he could attack, the Saintess attacked using the flying swords again.
’She is underestimating me,’ Kent said inwardly as he defended against the three swords. The battle hadn’t even started yet, and she had already begun looking down on him.
It was as if she had everything figured out, and to her, Kent was merely a bug in front of her. She wasn’t even putting in much effort, yet she thought she could defeat him easily.
’Well then...’ Kent blinked, distancing himself from her.

chapters.title: Chapter 262: Kent vs Sword Saintess Val (2)
paragraphs: It was as if not being taken seriously was not something Kent wanted.
He clearly hated that, considering just watching the Saintess behave like she wasn’t putting in much effort pissed him off, so Kent chose to add some heat to the battle.
He blinked away and held his sword sheath with his left hand while his right hand gripped the hilt.
Suddenly, a light flashed, and 36 deadly sharp strings appeared in the air.
The Saintess, who had been using the flying swords, suddenly felt the danger, so she tapped into her sword qi and executed her attack.
She saw that playing around would land her in hot waters.
The strings clashed, sending shockwaves here and there. The attack wasn’t that strong per standards, but it was enough to take care of a Grandmaster.
This was Kent’s way of saying, you better woman up and face me like a lady...
"Again," Kent unleashed the attack once more, sending 36 strings, this time using both sword qi and intent. However, she defended like the first one.
But the attack became deadlier, shocking the Saintess, who recognized the energy she had just defended against.
"Again," Kent shouted, this time making it 48 strings. The Saintess used all three flying swords and her handheld sword to defend, pushing her back slightly.
"You might want to put in the effort, else you will lose—and lose bitterly too," Kent said.
He blinked away, and the next time he appeared, his sword was out of the sheath, causing the energy around him to surge. The sword sheath vanished into his soul sea.
Lightning danced around the sword and his arms.
The Sword Saintess also unleashed her profound intent and qi when she felt how powerful Kent had become after drawing his sword.

Kent moved, becoming a blur. All that could be seen was a streak of lightning moving around the battleground. The blades clashed, and Kent and the Saintess finally began to exert their strength in close combat.
The clash of steel echoed like thunder, each strike sending ripples of energy that tore through the air.
Kent’s movements were precise, his blade a flash of lightning that seemed to cut through space itself.
The Saintess, though initially caught off guard, matched his ferocity, her sword qi swirling around her like a storm.
Her three flying swords darted around her, weaving a deadly dance as they intercepted Kent’s relentless attacks.

The disciples watching were all taken aback by how ferocious the battle had become. They all expected Kent to lose in under a minute. But the flashing and blade clashes echoing in the arena just don’t feel like he was losing at all.
On the contrary, he matched the saintess and even made it so she couldn’t do anything to him as she had hoped.
He has undistributed points, after all...
Kent was pushed back, causing him to exhale, but the next second, he was upon the Saintess.
He dashed forward, his sword slicing horizontally in a wide arc. The Saintess blocked, but the force of the blow sent her skidding back, her feet carving grooves into the ground.
Kent was running while teleporting at the same time. So, the attacks coming from the flying swords are just attacking his afterimage.
His body flickered, and he reappeared above her, bringing his sword down in a vertical slash. The Saintess raised her blade, the impact resonating like a gong.
The ground beneath her cracked, but she held firm, her expression unreadable.
Suddenly, her three flying swords shot toward Kent from different angles, forcing him to retreat.
He twisted mid-air, deflecting two of the swords with quick, precise strikes, but the third grazed his arm, drawing a thin line of blood.
Kent smirked, glancing at the wound before locking eyes with the Saintess.
Of course, the disciples who saw this all cheered, believing the first cut was the step to trashing him.
"I was careless there," Kent muttered loud enough for the saints to hear.
However, she didn’t respond.
Instead, she raised her hand, and the flying swords returned to her side, orbiting her like loyal guardians.
She held a calm expression on her face, but inwardly, she was shocked that Kent was still standing.
Her sword qi intensified, the air around her shimmering with power.
She stepped forward with calculated and calm steps and swung her blade. A wave of qi erupted from the strike, racing toward Kent with terrifying speed.
Kent didn’t dodge. He met the attack head-on, his sword cutting through the wave and dispersing it into harmless sparks.
But the Saintess was already on the move, instantly closing the distance between them.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
Their blades met again, metal clashing and filling the air as they exchanged a flurry of strikes. Each movement was calculated, and each strike aimed to exploit an opening.
Inside the VIP room, Saintess Mara held a calm expression, but inwardly, she was shocked by how Kent was handling the battle. It was like he was matched with the Saintess.
Suddenly, her eyes widened when Kent unleashed an attack after breaking the close combat. From what he had observed, the Saintess was good at the close combat.
So when Kent broke away, she knew he also saw that and decided to change the battle style.
But the close combat helped him add 5000 points to all the right places.
Now, he was much faster than before, but the Saintess was no pushover. So, the strategy changed, and this strategy was what he was going to use against the clone.
"Rapid Slash," Kent unleashed the attack, sending 100 sword arcs flying at the Saintess, who was forced to move back and distance herself from Kent.
"Don’t run, I am just getting started," Kent said with a smirk.
He unleashed another, filling the air with 100 Sword arcs, each speeding toward the saintess, who did a 360 swing, sending a gust of wind flying at Kent.
Then she moved through the chaos that appeared behind Kent. She stabbed forward, but before it could land on him, Kent vanished and appeared a couple of meters away.
"Rapid Slash." This time, 200 sword arcs appeared, causing everyone to widen their eyes. The air was filled with beautiful golden arcs.
But instead of admiring their beauty, they were now aiming to claim the Saintess’ life. Even a blind man could see that.
The golden arcs are, without a doubt, beautiful to the eye, but they are deadly to anyone. One cannot admire them simply because they are not meant to be admired.
She started to see her shortcomings. But she must first break even, considering Kent wasn’t stopping his attacks.
He was using the chances he had to unleash a flurry of attacks on the Saintess, making it so she couldn’t get close.
Suddenly, the energy around the Saintess also changed, causing Kent to move back. The intent around her now was much more powerful, causing him to take a cold breath.
’And so it began...the attacks that will determine who wins.’ Kent knew she was about to make her move, so he was prepared for it.
The Saintess defended against the sword arcs, and she pointed forward. The three swords moved.
